title: SAE Interventions are Unreliable: Post-Intervention Recovery of Suppressed Behavior

data.title: SAE Interventions are Unreliable: Post-Intervention Recovery of Suppressed Behavior
data.research_question: Can a behavior suppressed by an SAE feature clamp be recovered from the defended residual state while the clamp remains active and targeted features stay near defended values?

models_and_data.item: TPP official layer-5 benchmark on Gemma-scale model with Gemma-Scope residual SAE
models_and_data.quote: We use the official layer-5 TPP benchmark without modifying its feature-selection or ablation pipeline.

models_and_data.item: WMDP-Bio unlearning with SAE-based biology feature clamping
models_and_data.quote: We use the SAE-based WMDP-Bio unlearning setting, where biology-related SAE features are selected from forget-versus-retain statistics and clamped during inference to suppress target-domain answer accuracy.

models_and_data.item: IOI circuit-level test on GPT-2 Small with residual SAE
models_and_data.quote: For GPT-2 Small, we select SAE features with positive attribution to this IO-minus-S logit difference, clamp them while preserving the SAE reconstruction residual, and optimize a residual recovery variable at the defended answer position.

models_and_data.item: Refusal recovery on strict valid AdvBench prompts with Gemma-2B refusal SAE features
models_and_data.quote: We evaluate on strict valid AdvBench prompts: the unclamped model must produce a non-refusal response, while the active refusal clamp must turn the same prompt into a refusal under the same detector.
Appendix D repeats the protocol on HarmBench-Test and obtains 43/43 non-refusal recovery under low defended-feature drift.

models_and_data.item: Refusal feature-set size sweep on full 520-prompt AdvBench slice
models_and_data.quote: We construct feature sets of increasing size from the same local-union refusal-feature pool and evaluate each K on the full 520-prompt AdvBench slice.

protocol.step: Restrict recovery evaluation to valid flips where the base model shows the behavior and the active SAE intervention suppresses it
protocol.quote: We evaluate recovery only on valid flips: examples where the base model exhibits the target behavior but the active SAE intervention suppresses it.

protocol.step: Start from the clamped defended residual state and optimize small residual perturbations
protocol.quote: Starting from the clamped state, we optimize small residual perturbations to restore the target behavior.

protocol.step: Approximate the constrained recovery search with projected gradient descent
protocol.quote: We therefore approximate the search using projected gradient descent (PGD).

protocol.step: For single-layer interventions, project updates away from selected SAE encoder directions
protocol.quote: For single-layer interventions, we project updates away from the selected SAE encoder directions.

protocol.step: For cross-layer interventions, use feature-map Jacobians to constrain feature changes across layers
protocol.quote: For cross-layer interventions, we use feature-map Jacobians to constrain how perturbations affect the features across layers.

protocol.step: Replay four components under the active clamp for recovery-path attribution
protocol.quote: For each optimized perturbation, we replay four components under the same active clamp: clamped-feature changes, non-clamped SAE-feature changes, top-k non-clamped feature changes, and the SAE reconstruction residual.

protocol.step: Report recovery rate as behavioral metric and activation drift as defended-feature violation metric
protocol.quote: Unless otherwise stated, we report recovery rate as the behavioral metric and activation drift as the primary defended-feature violation metric.

key_results.claim: Encoder-orthogonal TPP recovery preserves high behavioral recovery while sharply restricting targeted-feature reactivation.
key_results.quote: At the latent level, TPP on SAEBench [10] shows that encoder-orthogonal recovery preserves a high behavioral recovery rate of 74.9% while sharply restricting targeted-feature reactivation to just 0.002.

key_results.claim: WMDP-Bio unlearning recovery restores strict valid answer-choice flips with zero measured activation drift.
key_results.quote: At the output level, WMDP-Bio unlearning [8] demonstrates that recovery restores 98.9% of strict valid answer-choice flips from the post-intervention state with zero measured activation drift.

key_results.claim: Encoder-projected IOI recovery achieves full recovery with low reactivated-feature fraction.
key_results.quote: At the circuit level, IOI [22] shows that the encoder-projected method achieves 100% recovery with only a 0.016 reactivated-feature fraction.

key_results.claim: Refusal-steering recovery is high while defended-feature relative drift remains low.
key_results.quote: Especially in the safety-critical refusal-steering setting, we achieve a 95.8% recovery rate on valid samples while keeping defended-feature relative drift to 0.131, substantially below suffix-based baselines.

key_results.claim: SAE reconstruction residual is the main recovery carrier.

key_results.claim: HarmBench-Test shows non-refusal recovery under low defended-feature drift.
key_results.quote: Appendix D repeats the protocol on HarmBench-Test and obtains 43/43 non-refusal recovery under low defended-feature drift.

key_results.claim: Recovery remains high with larger refusal feature sets in the stable range.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Not a universal impossibility result for SAE-based interventions.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Our results are not a universal impossibility result for SAE-based interventions.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Results depend on feature selection and SAE release.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: They are feature-selection and SAE-release dependent: the tested defenses act on selected SAE features in specific dictionaries and model settings.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Broader evaluation across models, prompts, clamp strengths, and SAE releases is needed.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Therefore, broader evaluation across models, prompts, clamp strengths, and SAE releases is needed to determine the full scope of the phenomenon.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Manual labels are pending, so opening-category diagnostics are automatic rather than independent human evaluation.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Manual labels are pending, so this table should be interpreted as an automatic diagnostic rather than an independent human evaluation.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The recovery optimizer may exploit implementation-specific artifacts of the SAE clamp, decoder geometry, or perturbation parameterization rather than a general behavioral bypass; the paper does not ablate clamp implementation details or decoder non-orthogonality.

Automatic refusal and safety-cue detectors are used for strict-valid filtering and recovery scoring; manual labels are pending, so reported refusal recovery may overstate true harmful or base-like behavior.

Most experiments use small strict-valid subsets and single runs; the paper does not report multiple random seeds, optimizer hyperparameter sweeps, or stability across PGD/Jacobian projection settings.

The cross-layer Jacobian projection is a first-order local approximation; higher-order or nonlinear feature changes may evade the preservation constraints, so defended-feature drift may underestimate true reactivation.

The white-box per-example optimization with gradient access and a perturbation budget may not match realistic deployment constraints; the paper does not test black-box, query-limited, or compute-limited attackers.
The models are Gemma-scale/Gemma-2B and GPT-2 Small, not Gemma 4 E2B or KV-shared layers 15-34; transfer to the lab's architecture and CPU tracing setup is untested.
Recovery-path attribution uses behavioral replay of non-orthogonal SAE decoder components; the paper acknowledges norms are not variance fractions but does not fully rule out component interference.
data.relevance_to_lab: Useful as a caution and diagnostic template for activation patching/logit-lens work: it tests whether a clamped SAE feature is a complete bottleneck and attributes recovery to the SAE reconstruction residual, with encoder-orthogonal and cross-layer Jacobian projections that could inform tracing across KV-shared layers. It does not study Gemma 4 E2B, layers 15-34, per-layer embeddings, induction heads, or factual recall, and its GPU-based per-example optimization would need adaptation for CPU tracing.

key_results.claim: Encoder projection preserved substantial TPP target recovery while sharply reducing defended-feature reopening.
key_results.quote: Encoder projection reduces target-mean recovery from 0.819 to 0.749, but sharply lowers post-hoc evidence of feature reopening: mean reactivation drops from 0.013 to 0.002.

key_results.claim: WMDP-Bio answer behavior remained almost fully recoverable from the defended state despite zero measured activation drift.
key_results.numbers: 98.9% recovery; 90/91 answer-choice flips; zero measured activation drift.
key_results.quote: At the output level, WMDP-Bio unlearning [8] demonstrates that recovery restores 98.9% of strict valid answer-choice flips from the post-intervention state with zero measured activation drift.

key_results.claim: Encoder-projected IOI recovery restored every valid decision while scarcely reactivating the selected features.
key_results.quote: At the circuit level, IOI [22] shows that the encoder-projected method achieves 100% recovery with only a 0.016 reactivated-feature fraction.

key_results.claim: Jacobian-projected refusal recovery restored most strict-valid AdvBench behavior while keeping defended-feature movement low.
key_results.quote: Finally, in the safety refusal-steering task [16, 23], recovery reaches 95.8% on strict-valid AdvBench prompts while keeping defended-feature relative drift to 0.131.

key_results.claim: The refusal-recovery pattern generalized to HarmBench-Test, although base-response fidelity was substantially lower than non-refusal recovery.
key_results.numbers: 43/43 non-refusal recovery; 19/43 base-like recovery; 14/43 strict-base-like recovery.
key_results.quote: Jacobian-projected recovery restores non-refusal behavior on all 43 valid examples, with 19/43 base-like recoveries and 14/43 strict-base-like recoveries.

key_results.claim: Recovery remained high across the stable range of larger refusal-feature clamps.
key_results.quote: For K = 5–20, non-refusal recovery remains between 93.3% and 100.0%, while base-like recovery remains between 68.9% and 88.2%.

key_results.claim: The SAE-unexplained reconstruction residual, rather than reopened clamped features or a small set of alternative latents, was the dominant recovery carrier.
key_results.numbers: SAE residual replay: 23/24 non-refusal and 14/24 base-like; clamped-feature replay: 0/24 and 0/24; non-clamped SAE-feature replay: 2/24 and 1/24.
key_results.quote: Residual replay nearly matches full recovery, while clamped-feature replay fails and non-clamped SAE-feature replay remains weak.

key_results.claim: Encoder-projected WMDP recovery emerged with a modest perturbation budget and remained at zero measured defended-feature drift.
key_results.numbers: Budgets 0 and 2: no recovery; budget 5: 4/6; budget 10: 6/6; budget 20: no further increase; defended-feature drift zero.
key_results.quote: Encoder-projected recovery does not recover at budgets 0 or 2, partially recovers at budget 5 (4/6), and reaches full recovery at budget 10 (6/6), while maintaining zero measured defended-feature drift throughout.

limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Our results are not a universal impossibility result for SAE-based interventions.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Observed recovery is dependent on the selected features, SAE release, dictionary, and model setting.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: They are feature-selection and SAE-release dependent: the tested defenses act on selected SAE features in specific dictionaries and model settings.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The procedure is a white-box diagnostic rather than a black-box attack.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Our recovery procedure is a white-box diagnostic rather than a black-box attack.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Recovery requires internal activation and gradient access and uses per-input residual optimization.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: It assumes access to internal activations and gradients and optimizes per-input residual perturbations.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The results should not be interpreted as a directly deployable jailbreak.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: This is appropriate for testing intervention completeness, but it should not be interpreted as a directly deployable jailbreak.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Strict refusal filtering leaves a relatively small main set of clean recovery examples.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Finally, the refusal case study uses a strict valid-filtering protocol, which improves interpretability but leaves a relatively small main set of clean recovery examples.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: A non-refusal opening does not guarantee a coherent or original-answer response.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: a non-refusal output may still be degenerate, malformed, or unrelated to the original answer.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: An independent human evaluation of the refusal outputs has not yet been completed.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: This diagnostic is not a substitute for a full independent human evaluation; manual labels are still pending.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: Objective leakage and metric gaming are possible because optimization targets behavior while refusal evaluation relies partly on lexical opening detectors; a successful non-refusal readout may not imply coherent harmful-content recovery.
Valid-flip conditioning selects only cases where the intervention successfully suppresses behavior, creating selection bias and limiting population-level estimates of defense robustness.
Gradient-based per-input residual search may find adversarial off-manifold states, so recovered paths need not resemble trajectories the model would naturally take without an optimizer.

Encoder orthogonality and the local feature-map Jacobian constrain only first-order local feature motion; nonlinear cross-layer effects or long-generation drift may remain despite low post-hoc measurements.

The residual attribution identifies where behaviorally sufficient signal travels but does not establish whether it represents a stable semantic capability, prompt-specific artifacts, or optimization byproducts.
Heterogeneous models, SAE releases, intervention layers, tasks, and small strict-valid sets limit extrapolation to architectures and regimes not directly tested, including Gemma 4 E2B.
Per-example PGD and Jacobian computations may scale poorly, potentially limiting exhaustive auditing and practical deployment of the diagnostic.
data.relevance_to_lab: High methodological but moderate direct-model relevance. The paper's residual-stream SAE clamping, encoder-orthogonal activation patching, cross-layer Jacobian projection, and residual replay/knockout attribution map closely onto Gemma 4 E2B activation patching and per-layer embedding audits. It does not directly test Gemma 4 E2B, KV-shared layers 15-34, logit-lens analysis, induction-head or factual-recall tracing, or CPU execution; per-input PGD and Jacobian optimization would require a CPU-efficient adaptation and could be computationally expensive.
